tagKindNote: Every earlier release tag in this repository is annotated; v0.2.0-rc.13 was cut as a lightweight tag. It was kept as pushed instead of being deleted and recreated, because recreating a tag under an already published Release risks the release/tag association and would re-trigger the release workflow, whose overwrite guard refuses to touch a published release. The tag resolves to the same commit as the release target and the provenance check passes.
mainCommitMeaning: main was pushed to the release commit before the tag was pushed, so the release was cut on an already published branch commit
note: The pinned artifact was built from f7c9a2f (the documentation commit, which carries the six consistency fixes and the re-pinned documentation). 513ffac is the release commit: it only adds the pinned tarball, release/manifest.json, release/SHA256SUMS and the rewritten host acceptance evidence, and it changes no file inside the package allow-list. Nothing was rebuilt for the tag.

ci.ciHostAcceptanceNote: The CI runner repacks with the npm bundled with Node 22.19.0, so its tarball bytes differ from the pinned ones (c8c7a0a3...); the job asserts the recorded contentSha256 equals the pin, which is the environment-independent value.

noLatestRelease.meaning: every published release is a pre-release, so the repository has no latest release and an RC cannot be mistaken for a stable channel

packageUnchangedAfterPublication.statement: The published bytes and the pinned content were re-checked after the release; no file inside the package allow-list changed between the source commit and the release commit.

verificationLimits: The acceptance harness ran on macOS arm64 with Node v26.12.0; the CI run covers the same content on ubuntu-latest with Node 22.19.0 and 24.x.
CI host acceptance repacks with Node 22 npm, so its bytes differ from the pinned ones; only the content digest is compared there, as documented in RELEASE.md section 1.
Only 0.2.1-rc.2 was re-accepted against the anonymously downloaded bytes; the other two hosts were accepted locally against the pinned tarball and in CI against the same content.
remainingRisksAndUnverified: The event-bridge tail repair is a check-then-act over a file no writer locks: an append landing between the final read and the rename can still be dropped. The repair re-reads and refuses when the file changed while it was prepared; RELEASE.md risk 14, COMPATIBILITY.md and the README recovery table state the boundary.

The trusted event-bridge writer is read from an in-session config, else from the composed profile dump, else the bundle default; a writer that the dump states in a form this reader cannot read exactly (tag, template, inline config, duplicate key, duplicate entry, non-canonical key spelling) is reported as unknown (degraded) instead of guessed.

satisfiesRange() compares pre-release identifiers with localeCompare, so a multi-digit pre-release ordinal orders wrongly (satisfiesRange("1.0.0-rc.10", ">=1.0.0-rc.2") is false). Not fixed; the verified host combinations do not exercise it. RELEASE.md risk 15.
The released tag v0.2.0-rc.13 is lightweight while every earlier release tag is annotated (see tagKindNote).
